item.title: S&P 500 Earnings Growth Is Built on Unsustainable Foundations
item.description: Has the stock market bubble quietly burst already? Even though the S&P 500 Index has mostly treaded water for the past four months, Wall Street analysts have continued to boost their earnings estimates. This has left the benchmark trading at some its cheapest levels of recent years based on the so-called forward price-earnings, or P/E, ratio. And yet, it’s hard to call stocks a bargain, mostly because it’s “E” and not the “P” that looks increasingly unsustainable.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Levin

item.title: The End of Private Equity’s Leveraged Buyout Era Is Nigh
item.description: Higher-for-longer interest rates are forcing buyout firms to face facts. Struggling since 2023 to sell companies purchased in the long decade of ultra-cheap debt before the Covid pandemic, they’ve tried to placate investors with clever financial engineering to help keep some money turning over. But after several false dawns for a return to low rates, the classic private-equity leveraged deals industry is moving into the final stage of grief over its prospects: acceptance.
item.dc:creator: Paul J. Davies

item.title: Talarico Is Too Left for Texas and Paxton Is Too Amoral
item.description: At an intersection near our house in Dallas, one home has a large Talarico sign in the front yard. The home directly across the street has a large Paxton sign. That’s what it’s like down here one month before Election Day. The candidates are neck-and-neck. Votes are split across streets and among families.
item.dc:creator: Abby McCloskey

item.title: Americans and Their Banks Depend on Strong Deposit Insurance
item.description: Banks in the US have plenty to celebrate these days, from record profits and higher stock prices to a strong economy and easier regulation. One thing they don’t need is an added discount on their deposit insurance — a crucial buffer that should be reinforced when times are good.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: Amazon Drivers’ Smart Glasses Are Going to Be an Image Problem
item.description: Coming soon up a garden path near you: an Amazon.com Inc. driver wearing smart glasses, almost constantly taking pictures and sending them back to the company to be analyzed by humans and fed into an AI system.
item.dc:creator: Dave Lee

item.title: Obsolete Office Buildings Open a Path for Downtown Transformations
item.description: In March 1836, businessman and former New York City Mayor Philip Hone noted in his diary that he had sold his house on Broadway across from City Hall Park for $60,000 ($2.2 million in current dollars) with the buyer planning to convert it into shops and a hotel. “Almost everybody down-town is in the same predicament, for all the dwellinghouses are to be converted into stores,” Hone wrote. “We are tempted with prices so exorbitantly high that none can resist.”
item.dc:creator: Justin Fox

item.title: The Intangible Economy Is Making Everyone Miserable
item.description: These are the best of times for Americans — at least economically and at least on paper (in the metaphorical sense of course, since no one uses paper anymore). We’ve never been richer or more prosperous as a nation. Living standards and life expectancy are at all-time highs. Yet, it feels like the economy is broken.
item.dc:creator: Allison Schrager

item.title: The Big Bond Market Shift Is Impacting Europe
item.description: The shifts in bond investors’ sentiment have created a much more difficult environment for Europe’s governments and companies.
item.dc:creator: John Authers

item.title: Why Is Oil at $100 If Trump Is Winning the Battle in Hormuz?
item.description: I don’t know who will win the US-Iran war. But if you ask me who’s prevailing in the battle over the Strait of Hormuz, it’s clear US President Donald Trump has the advantage. As much as Tehran says the opposite, the strait is effectively wide open. Crude oil exports from regional US allies via the waterway, plus bypass routes, have risen to about 80% of prewar levels. Iran, meanwhile, has seen its own oil exports plunge to zero.
item.dc:creator: Javier Blas

item.title: Sweden Gives Hope to Real Conservatives Everywhere
item.description: Ulf Kristersson’s Moderates, who’ve spent four years leading Sweden’s governing coalition, did what voters wanted. The center-right party got growth going: It’s expected to be 2.5% for 2026 and 2027, remarkable for a European nation. Inflation is 0.3%, and — of greater importance to plenty of Swedes — asylum applications this year will be the lowest since 1985. They’ve even started building nuclear power plants again.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Sharma

item.title: Manchester City Nightmare Is a Dream for Its American Rivals in Premier League
item.description: Manchester City has been found guilty of systematically breaking Premier League rules for almost a decade, in a watershed for the world’s richest football competition. The verdicts taint the legacy of England’s most successful club over the past 15 years, and by extension the sport’s reputation.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Brooker

item.title: Appalachian Coal Miners Battle a Black Lung Renaissance
item.description: Nobody wants another generation toiling in the coal mines, and yet that’s exactly where things are headed.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Karl

item.title: India Has the Solar. Can It Power the AI Boom?
item.description: Nobody will be surprised if within the next five to 10 years India displaces the US as the world’s second-largest solar grid after China. But if its ambition is to become the world’s factory — or host AI workloads for Western tech giants — the power play around energy must stop.
item.dc:creator: Andy Mukherjee

item.title: UK Pension Triple Lock Is Only the Start for Andy Burnham
item.description: “This is the deal,” Andy Burnham declared as he used his first speech to the Labour Party annual conference as prime minister to promise a new national-care system for the UK funded by scrapping the “triple lock” pension ratchet. His “deal,” of course, went much further than just facing down retirees. He grabbed the moment to make the intellectual and moral case for a more expansive state.
item.dc:creator: Rosa Prince
